about: The 1989 village shop counter that replaced the vanilla yellow market cart CounterShop_01: a neutral oak carcass with three recessed veneer panels in a darker frame (stiles, rails and bevelled mouldings), a moulded top rail, a brushed steel kick plate, a beige speckled laminate top with a steel edge, open clerk shelves with kraft bags and a wrapping-paper roll. ShopCounterTill adds a 1980s electromechanical cash register (terraced round keys, colored department keys, a long TOTAL bar, a hand crank, a journal window with a slip, a CASH drawer with a brass lock, a pop-up AMOUNT tower readable from both sides), a service bell, a receipt spike with slips and a THANK YOU change mat. Built by build.py in headless Blender with kitlib and procedural textures; all printed text US English, no brand, no place name.

layout_m.about: Enfusion metres, x right, y up, z forward. The footprint is the vanilla CounterShop_01 it replaces (x -0.75..0.75, y 0..1.039, z -0.525..0.597, same origin), so every placed counter keeps its seat and everything standing on it keeps its height. The customer front is +z; the clerk stands on the -z side (Saint-Philippe bakery clerk 0.98 m behind the origin).

emissive.about: The till's figure display glows faintly green.
